items.derivation: The line has gradient 5. At contact f'(x)=5, so 4x-3=5 and x=2; the line then gives y=3. Integrating gives f(x)=2x^2-3x+C. Substituting (2,3) gives 3=8-6+C, hence C=1. Differentiation returns 4x-3; f(2)=3 and f'(2)=5, confirming the supplied line is tangent at (2,3).
items.methodScope: The booklet explicitly teaches a tangent gradient as a derivative condition and finding a specific primitive from a point. Solving the supplied derivative equal to the supplied line slope for the unknown contact x, then reading its y from the line, is ordinary algebraic transfer of the tangent-gradient relation, not a new integration method. The bounded examples supply contact coordinates, so this exact inference is not demonstrated there; an identical example is not required.
